tagline.text: A pilgrimage hill park in Ligao where the Stations of the Cross wind around a cauldron-shaped crater

location.label: Location
location.text: Barangay Tuburan (California Village), Ligao City, Albay, about 30km south of Legazpi

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: February–May dry season (crowded during Holy Week)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱10~1,000 (free entry; parking, ATV and donations optional; transport not included)

children.text: Kawa-Kawa Hill is a hill about 236m high in Ligao, Albay, whose summit is a cauldron-shaped (kawa) depression, which is why it is called the "hill without a hilltop." It is both a pilgrimage site, with life-size Stations of the Cross sculptures along the climb and around the crater, and a nature park with views of Mayon Volcano.
Kawa-Kawa Hill is a hill in Barangay Tuburan (also called California Village), Ligao City, Albay. It lies about
south of Legazpi, so it is not in Legazpi itself, but it is widely described as a day trip from Legazpi. The hill stands about
above sea level and is said to be about
5.8km

from the foothills of Mayon Volcano. The name "kawa" means cauldron in Bikol, and the hill was named for the way its top sinks into a round, cauldron-like bowl. With no peak and a crater-like depression of about 6 hectares at the top, it is also nicknamed "a hill without a hilltop."
Its biggest draw is that it is a place of pilgrimage. Along a paved climb of about

from the foot of the hill to the crater, life-size statues form the Stations of the Cross, and more statues continue along the path around the crater rim. Most guides say that of the 14 stations, 6 are on the ascent and 8 are around the crater. One travel blog, however, lists 10 stations, so the number varies by source; please check on site. The sculptures are said to be the work of a sculptor from Paete, Laguna, and near the start of the path you will find a Last Supper statue and the Divine Mercy Monastery of Carmelite nuns, built in 2014.
The path around the crater is described as about

long, and from the rim you can see Mayon Volcano, Mt. Masaraga, and the farmland and rooftops of Ligao in one sweep. The walk is short. One blogger wrote that it took less than 20 minutes to reach the top. That makes it easy for families without much physical strain, and many pilgrims walk it slowly in prayer. For photographers, the appeal is the green grass inside the crater with Mayon Volcano in the distance, all in one frame.

Inside the crater there are ATV rides and horseback riding, and some sources mention sunflower and flower gardens and bird aviaries. Birdwatchers have recorded species such as the yellow-vented bulbul, striated grassbird and collared kingfisher. Entry is free and donation boxes are provided; only parking is charged separately. The park is privately owned and said to be managed by a group linked to an Albay congressman, but it is open to the public. Opening hours and facilities differ by source, so check locally. Note also that the Wikivoyage entry has not been updated since November 2020.

Life-size statues line the climb and the crater rim. Most guides say there are 6 stations on the ascent and 8 around the crater. You do not need to be Catholic to enjoy walking among the sculptures, and the stations double as rest stops.
The summit is not a peak but a hollow of about 6 hectares, hence the name "hill without a hilltop." Walk the rim path (about
) in a full loop to see the scenery both inside and outside the crater.

blocks.title: Views of Mayon Volcano and Mt. Masaraga

children.text: From the crater rim you can see Mayon Volcano and Mt. Masaraga. Guides say the view is clearest in the early morning or late afternoon when there are fewer clouds, but clouds can hide them depending on the weather.
One source says ATV rides in the crater cost ₱100 for about
15 minutes
. Horseback riding is also reportedly offered, but I could not confirm the price, so ask on site.

blocks.title: Footprint donation on the brick steps

children.text: You can reportedly leave a footprint or handprint on a brick step by donating
to the church. This is entirely optional, so confirm availability and the amount locally.
During Lent and Holy Week, many pilgrims climb the hill. This is the busiest time: good if you want to experience the atmosphere of the observance, but better avoided if you want a quiet walk.

Birdwatchers watch for birds in the crater and on the slopes, and depending on the season, gardens of sunflowers or cosmos are reportedly planted. Birds and flowers vary by season, so keep your expectations modest.

items.title: 1–2 hour course
items.subtitle: The Stations of the Cross and a loop of the crater

children.text: Park at the entrance (guides list ₱10 for motorcycles and ₱20 for cars) and check the restrooms and rest area.
See the Last Supper statue in front of the monastery and walk up the paved climb. Take your time at stations 1 to 6 along the ascent.
Reach the crater rim, look out to Mayon Volcano and Mt. Masaraga, and take photos.
Follow the rim path past the remaining 8 stations. The rim path is about
Come back down and buy Bicolano snacks or pili nuts at the stalls, or try an activity such as the ATV.
The climb is short, but the pavement is slippery when wet, so wear shoes with good grip.

items.title: Day trip from Legazpi
items.subtitle: Ligao pilgrimage and the Mayon Volcano area

children.text: Take a van or bus bound for Ligao from the Legazpi Grand Central Terminal. Guides say it takes about 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Get off in Ligao town (near the public market) and take a tricycle to Kawa-Kawa Hill.
Walk the Stations of the Cross and the crater rim path.
Have lunch in Ligao town and return to Legazpi.
If you have time, visit Cagsawa Ruins or Daraga Church in the Legazpi area.
There are domestic flights from Manila to Bicol International Airport (DRP) in Daraga. Airlines and schedules change by season, so check when booking.
From the airport, head into Legazpi and then continue to Ligao as described below.
Guides suggest taking a long-distance bus from Manila to Legazpi and asking the conductor to drop you off in Ligao. Travel time varies greatly with traffic, so check with the bus company.
In Ligao town, take a jeepney or tricycle to Kawa-Kawa Hill.
From Legazpi Grand Central Terminal, a UV Express van or bus signed "Ligao," "Polangui" or "Libon" reportedly takes about
45 minutes to 1 hour
to reach Ligao town. Vans reportedly leave about every 30 minutes or when full.
Another guide says to take a jeepney from downtown Legazpi toward Ligao, Oas or Polangui, get off at Tuburan (near the Seventh Day Adventist Church), and switch to a tricycle.
From the Ligao terminal or town center (near the public market) it is about
2.5km
to Kawa-Kawa Hill, and guides say a tricycle takes about
5~10 minutes
. I could not confirm the fare, so agree on the price before you ride.
Public transport is limited, and some guides recommend renting a car or hiring one with a driver.
From Naga Central Bus Terminal, take a bus or van bound for Ligao, Legazpi or Polangui and get off in Ligao town. Guides say it takes about
2.5~3.5 hours

Since the walk is short and the experience is mostly outdoor scenery, the drier months are best. Some guides recommend the cooler early morning (4:30–6:30) or late afternoon (4:00–6:00). There is little shade, so avoid midday.

During Lent and Holy Week, pilgrims crowd the hill and it is at its busiest of the year. If you want a quiet walk, pick a weekday outside Lent; if you want to see the pilgrimage atmosphere, go during this period. A reader comment says the hill was open during Holy Week, but check announcements for events.
In the rainy and typhoon season, the paved climb is slippery and clouds can hide Mayon Volcano. Bicol lies in the path of typhoons, so check the weather forecast before you go.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: Good for views and walking; hot at midday; crowded during Holy Week in March–April
Steps and paths are slippery; Mayon Volcano is often hidden by clouds
Build slack into your schedule and aim for clear early mornings

There are few large lodgings around Kawa-Kawa Hill, so most visitors stay in Legazpi and make a day trip. Ligao town has modest places to stay, but Legazpi offers more tourist facilities and easier transport, so it is the safer base. Lodging prices vary by season, so check when you book.

Stalls near the entrance and the foot of the hill sell Bicolano snacks, pili nuts and souvenirs, and refill stations are reportedly available. For meals, it is easier to eat in Ligao town or back in Legazpi. Bicol's signature dishes are Bicol Express, made with coconut milk and hot chili, and laing (taro leaves in coconut milk).
Bring water, snacks, a hat and sunscreen; guides also suggest mosquito repellent.
The paved climb is slippery when it rains, so wear shoes with good soles.
Go in the early morning or late afternoon for cooler weather and better photos.
Carry small bills for parking, snacks and donations.
Take your trash with you and do not pick flowers or plants.
People are praying here, so do not shout or play loud music.
Guides say to get permission before flying a drone, so ask the park management first.
If your schedule allows, combine it with Mayon Volcano sights around Legazpi in one day.
Hours, facilities and prices differ by source and some sources are old, so check the latest announcements. Also check the Mayon Volcano alert level and the typhoon forecast.
The paved climb is slippery in the rain and some sections are steep, so older or less mobile visitors may need an aid or a companion.
The park is privately owned, and guides say activity facilities (ATV, horses and so on) are still being developed, so some may be closed. Confirm locally before making them the goal of your trip.
There is little shade and midday is very hot. Bring plenty of water.
An informal reply says camping may require permission from the local government, so ask in advance.
Ligao is some distance from Legazpi, so check the last ride back in advance.

Mayon Volcano
and its surroundings.
The ruins preserve the bell tower of a church buried by the 1814 eruption.
Cagsawa Ruins
is on the Legazpi side, so it can be combined into one day.
The old hilltop church
Daraga Church
is a good stop on the way back from Ligao to Legazpi.
Legazpi
, with lodging, restaurants and terminals, is the base for a trip to Kawa-Kawa Hill.
